title: Monotonic Array
prompt: An array is monotonic if it is either entirely non-increasing or entirely non-decreasing. Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if it is monotonic, or `false` otherwise.
hints: You don't need two separate passes — you can track both possibilities at once in a single scan.
Track two flags: whether the array could still be non-decreasing, and whether it could still be non-increasing.

As you scan, if any nums[i] > nums[i-1], the array cannot be non-increasing; if any nums[i] < nums[i-1], it cannot be non-decreasing. The array is monotonic if at least one flag survives the whole scan.

solution.approach: Maintain two booleans, is_increasing and is_decreasing, both starting true. Scan adjacent pairs: whenever a later element is smaller than the one before it, the array can't be non-decreasing, so clear is_increasing; whenever it's larger, clear is_decreasing. After the scan, the array is monotonic exactly when at least one of the two flags is still true, since that flag survived confirms that one direction held throughout.
